name: WholeBodyVLA
summary: WholeBodyVLA argues that splitting a humanoid into a manipulation policy and a locomotion controller is what caps task range, and that the fix is a single latent action space spanning both. A Latent Action Model learns unified latent actions from action-free egocentric video of manipulation and manipulation-aware locomotion, so ordinary human video supervises whole-body behaviour without any action annotation. A loco-manipulation-oriented RL policy then decodes those latents into stable whole-body coordination under disturbance. Demonstrated behaviours include bimanual grasping, side-stepping toward objects, squatting to place items, lifting boxes and pushing loads over 50 kg. Published at ICLR 2026 by Fudan, OpenDriveLab at HKU, AgiBot and SII.
innovation: One latent action space covering locomotion and manipulation, rather than two policies with an interface between them.
Action-free egocentric video as supervision for whole-body behaviour, not just for arm motion.
matters: The open, academic counterpart to Helix 02 and Gemini Robotics 2 — the same whole-body thesis, with the method and code published.
limits: Latent actions decoded through an RL policy inherit that policy's platform assumptions; transfer to other humanoids is untested.
Load and disturbance demonstrations are impressive but reported on a small task set.
lineage: LAPA's latent actions from action-free video, extended from arms to the whole body.
